readback.name: Poincare.DeTurckC2Covariance.differential_covariance
readback.mathematical_statement: All universal quantifiers range over arbitrary data, including an arbitrary universe u and manifold M. E is EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 3), Bilin is E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] ℝ, Jet1 is E →L[ℝ] Bilin, Jet2 is E →L[ℝ] Jet1, and Variables is (Bilin × Jet1) × Jet2. The leading letI binders fix the ordinary real operator-norm additive-group and real normed-space structures on Jet1, E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] E, E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] E →L[ℝ] E, and Jet2, fix the ordinary product normed-group and real normed-space structures on Bilin × Jet1 and Variables, and fix the ordinary product additive commutative monoid on Bilin × Jet1. Thus these derivative and equality expressions are evaluated using those specified canonical structures; they do not quantify over an arbitrary choice of norms. Let M have a topology, be Hausdorff, carry E charts, and be a C∞ manifold for 𝓡 3. Let g0 and bg be actual smooth Riemannian metrics: smooth tangent-bundle continuous bilinear forms, symmetric and strictly positive on nonzero tangent vectors, with the Riemannian boundedness condition. For arbitrary anchors anchor₁, anchor₂, arbitrary q : E → Bilin, and z : E, assume z is in chart₁.target, chart₁⁻¹(z) is in chart₂.source, the chosen chart₁ blending cutoff is identically 1 eventually near z, and the chosen chart₂ blending cutoff is identically 1 eventually near phi(z), where phi = chart₂ ∘ chart₁⁻¹. Also assume q is C² at phi(z) and its bilinear values are symmetric eventually near phi(z). No positivity of q or global regularity of q is assumed. For each anchor, set G0 equal to the actual chart metric of g0; set B equal to the chart Christoffel field of bg constructed globally from its chart metric blended with the Euclidean metric by the chosen cutoff; DB is its ordinary Fréchet derivative. DQ(anchor,r,y) is differential(B(y),DB(y),G0(y),DG0(y),D²G0(y)) applied to the actual two-jet ((r(y),Dr(y)),D²r(y)). Concretely, for input ((h,J),H), differential is the sum of (i) the inverse-matrix variation -Σᵢⱼₖₗ Aᵢₖ h(eₖ,eₗ) Aₗⱼ times H0(eᵢ,eⱼ), (ii) the positive principal contraction Σᵢⱼ Aᵢⱼ H(eᵢ,eⱼ), and (iii) the total Fréchet derivative with respect to (G,J) of lowerTerm(B,DB,G,J) at (G0,J0), applied to (h,J); A is the inverse matrix of G0 in the Euclidean basis. lowerTerm is explicitly -2 times the Ricci first-jet remainder plus the Lie first-jet remainder: metric advection J(W) and the two G slots involving the first-jet remainder of DW, where W is the inverse-metric contraction of the metric connection minus B. The background B and DB are fixed in this linearization. Thus the sign is the spatial DeTurck evolution sign -2 Ricci + Lie, with positive inverse-metric second-derivative contraction, and no time derivative or minus principal operator is present. Define Tq(y)(v,w) = q(phi(y))(Dphi(y)v,Dphi(y)w). The conclusion is pullback(DQ(anchor₂,q,phi(z)),Dphi(z)) = DQ(anchor₁,Tq,z), equivalently equality in every pair of tensor slots. This is a pointwise equality of these concrete finite-jet linear maps applied to the q two-jet. lowerDifferential is defined by total fderiv; the statement does not separately conclude a HasFDerivAt certificate for the full evolution, nor a uniform norm estimate or Banach-space mapping theorem. The cutoff-one zones and local symmetry are explicit hypotheses; neither differential covariance nor an overlap-jet equality is assumed. No compactness, topology of a closed simply connected manifold, metric family, or existence of a flow is asserted.
